P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Severely constrained. After August 2021, Afghanistan's international reserves, including banks' FX deposits at the central bank, were frozen, SWIFT and international settlements were suspended, and banks faced acute AFN and FX liquidity shortages. Some banks now advertise SWIFT transfers 'subject to availability'. Sanctions screening (UN, US and others) affects any cross-border payment.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Single captured source (UNDP brief, 2021-era) on 2026-10-22; current conditions not confirmed.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Business licences are issued by the Afghanistan Investment Support Agency (AISA) or the Ministry of Commerce. Persons without such a licence are taxed at 3% (versus 2% fixed tax for licensed importers).
L1_registration.note: Single secondary source on 2026-10-22; registration procedure under current authorities not captured.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: The Income Tax Law taxes Afghan-source income of all persons and the foreign income of Afghan residents. A person is resident if their principal home is in Afghanistan at any time in the fiscal year, among other tests. Individuals pay progressive rates. Revenue Department guidelines of 14 July 2026 reportedly raised the exempt threshold, removed the 2% bracket and cut corporate tax from 20% to 10%.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: National identity card: Tazkira (National Identity Document) (Wikipedia, compulsory-ID list). Banks and payment platforms usually also accept a passport; their exact lists were not captured.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
